info.desc: Definitely Maybe is the debut album from the British rock band Oasis, released in 1994 under the Creation label. It has received positive reviews from music magazines. The first single of the album, "Live Forever", was voted Best Brittish Song, by voters of the alternative rock station Xfm London. Allmusic states that in this album the best of Rock'n'Roll, from The Beatles to The Stone Roses are mixed together. It's one of the best selling debut albums ever. .

podcast.body: Oasis formed when Noel Gallagher — then a roadie for the Inspiral Carpets who wrote songs during downtime at his day job behind a British Gas parts counter — took over his brother Liam's band Rain and renamed it after a local venue. After singles "Columbia," "Supersonic," and "Shakermaker," their Creation Records debut *Definitely Maybe* dropped on August 29, 1994. It became the fastest-selling debut album in UK history at that point, moving 100,000 copies in four days and debuting at number one, outselling its nearest competitor by 50%. Critical acclaim was universal; worldwide sales eventually exceeded 10 million copies. Together with Blur's *Parklife*, it launched the Britpop era that consumed British music for the following years. "It had outsold its nearest competitor by 50%."

podcast.body: Released in August 1994, this debut album was met with explosive demand from the public. This demand was fueled by several months of successful singles that had consistently charted high and were widely purchased, building immense anticipation for the full-length record. The album solidified Oasis's distinct musical identity, drawing heavily from classic British rock influences, and was considered one of two "masterpieces" that defined the Britpop movement by early 1996. "la demanda es explosiva, porque la gente llevaba siete meses, seis meses escuchando single de Oasis que eran tremenos que estaban entrando en todos los top charts."

podcast.title: Debut Album
podcast.body: The artwork for Oasis's debut album, released in May 1994, was designed by Brian Cannon with photography by Michael Spencer Jones. It features the five band members in the front room of rhythm guitarist Paul "Bonehead" Arthurs' home in Didsbury, Manchester, an idea inspired by a Beatles compilation. The meticulously staged shot includes personal items, carefully chosen props, and features the album title in Cannon's own handwriting. "Artwork was important to Oasis from the very beginning."
